title: Inflight request leak & runtime deadlock sleuth notes
content:
Summary:

High-level: During a sustained traffic pattern with many short chats and a small median sequence length, a subset of hosts started accumulating inflight request state inside the serving runtime's request-tracking map. This growth correlated with CPU stall events and eventually host-level deadlocks where batching goroutines were blocked on a chained mutex while GC/cleanup tasks tried to scan the same inflight map. We observed out-of-memory and long-tail request latencies for affected capacity lanes.

Impact: ~8 hosts (10% of the cluster for that pool) entered degraded state across a 40-minute window; client error rate for the model route spiked to ~12% and P95 latency for generation jumped from 110ms to 1.3s in the worst window. No customer data was leaked; incidents were internal availability degradation only.

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-02-22 02:18 UTC: First alert - pool error rate > 5% for 3m (Alert: serving.route.error-rate).
- 02:22 UTC: Oncall paged. Initial triage shows high RSS and busy syscalls on several hosts.
- 02:30 UTC: Team attaches to host, sees many goroutines stuck in runtime/netpoll and in-flight bookkeeping paths.
- 02:38 UTC: Short-term mitigation - scale out pool + enable per-host request-shed; errors reduced but some hosts still rising in memory.
- 03:02 UTC: Found repeated log entry pattern 'inflight: add request id=...' without matching 'inflight: remove request id=...'.
- 03:20 UTC: Forced process restart on 5 hosts prior to rolling fix, incident improved.

Symptoms & observational evidence:
- Logs: repeated pairs missing; examples: inflight add for req 0x9f3ac then no corresponding remove for >20m.
- Stack traces: dumps show goroutines blocked on inflightMap.mu -> batchCoordinator.mu -> evictor.mu chain. GC sweeps often coincide with the period when the inflight map is large.
- Metrics: inflight_map_size{host=...} climbed from ~20 to ~4,800 on affected hosts. Memory RSS correlated with inflight_map_size.
- PromQL used: sum by (host) (serving_inflight_map_size{pool="gen-1"})
- Host syscalls: high futex contention measured by perf (see perf log attached in linked artifacts).

Hypotheses ranked (most to least likely):
1) Request lifecycle early-exit path missing remove: under certain error branches (rpc timeout vs client disconnect) the code increments inflight without decrementing, creating permanent entries until eviction; with batching and KV-cache prefetch path, these entries hold references to large KV chunks so RSS climbs.
2) Eviction/backpressure race: eviction attempts to remove keys while batching coordinator holds iteration lock; under GC pressure and long-running prefetch, the mutex order inversion creates deadlock cycle. This explains chained locks in traces.
3) Memory accounting bug: inflight entries get duplicated in a secondary map used for metrics, doubling references; less likely since duplication would be visible in map size accounting.

Reproduction steps (local harness attempted):
- Running load generator that opens many short-lived streams with intermittent cancels (curl-like) at ~1k rps across 50 clients.
- Injected artificial network drop on a random 1% of requests to force error paths.
- Observed inflight_map_size growth after 10-15 minutes in the harness, but at reduced scale vs prod; suggests timing dependency.
- Reproduce with race detector enabled to check for missing unlocks; test found inconsistent ordering in 1 run out of 250 runs.

Short-term mitigations applied during incident:
- Increased pool size (scale-out) to absorb requests while we investigated.
- Enabled per-host shed: reject new requests when inflight_map_size > 1000. This prevented other hosts from following the same path.
- Forced restarts on the most-affected hosts to free RSS and clear inflight state.
- Added temporary logging to record add/remove events with stack id for future correlation (deployed via hotfix PR 850).

Runbook draft: triage checklist (for future similar incidents)
- Pager lands: capture pool and route id, list affected hosts.
- Run: promql 'topk(10, sum by (host) (serving_inflight_map_size{pool="${pool}"}))' and note hosts > 1000.
- SSH to top host, capture: pstack, heap profile (pprof --alloc_objects), goroutine dump.
- Check logs for 'inflight: add' without matching 'remove' in last 15m.
- If inflight_map_size > 2000 and host unresponsive: consider restart after draining traffic (if on Dedicated, follow infra restart SOP).
- Apply temporary inbound-shed via dynconfig: shed threshold = 1000 for 30m; escalate to eng-sre lead.

Playbook commands/examples (copyable):
- Prometheus queries: topk(10,rate(serving_request_errors_total[5m])) and sum by(host) (serving_inflight_map_size).
- pprof snapshot (binary path is /opt/serving/bin/serving): curl -sS localhost:6060/debug/pprof/heap?seconds=5 > /tmp/heap.pb && go tool pprof -text /opt/serving/bin/serving /tmp/heap.pb
- goroutine dump: kill -QUIT <pid> or curl localhost:6060/debug/pprof/goroutine?debug=2 > /tmp/goroutines.txt
- quick stack search: grep -E "inflight|batchCoordinator|evictor" /tmp/goroutines.txt | sed -n '1,200p'

Mitigation attempted & outcome:
- Hotfix PR 850 adds defensive remove in several early-return branches in request lifecycle. Deployed as canary to 2 hosts; inflight growth stayed flat on canary while neighbor host grew.
- Temporary sheath threshold prevented cascade; however, we need permanent prevention for the root cause.

Longer-term actions (owner + ETA):
- (eng-serving-runtime) Formal code audit of inflight lifecycle. Owner: Samir. ETA: 2026-03-05.
- (eng-serving-runtime) Add invariant test harness that asserts add/remove counts converge after simulated cancellations. Owner: Jules. ETA: 2026-03-12.
- (eng-sre) Add alert: inflight_map_size per-host > 500 for 5m. Owner: Marcus. ETA: 2026-03-01.
- (eng-serving-runtime) Rework locking order to avoid mu inversion between inflightMap and batchCoordinator; prototype branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/862. Owner: Nora. ETA: 2026-04-01.

Outstanding questions & risks:
- Is there any customer-facing workload pattern that intentionally leaves requests hanging that we should rate-limit proactively?
- Effectiveness of eviction when inflight entries reference large KV payloads; eviction may need to free deeper references to actually reduce RSS.
- Risk of restarts during peak traffic for Dedicated customers; need a more graceful draining workflow.

Notes to self & follow-ups:
- Attach perf flamegraphs from affected hosts to SERV-4821.
- Confirm hotfix PR 850 covers all early-return paths; code owners to review.
- After closure: run chaos test that randomly cancels streams at 10% of requests for 30m to ensure invariants hold.

Slack trail & context: initial report by @nora via #sre-incidents at 02:20 UTC; internal postmortem will be drafted after all owners close actions.

Appendix: sample excerpt from goroutine dump (redacted):
 - goroutine 4821 [semacquire]:
    sync.runtime_SemacquireMutex+0x45
    sync.(*Mutex).Lock+0x9a
    runtime/inflight.(*Map).add+0x12f
    runtime/batching.(*Coordinator).enqueue+0x2a3
    runtime/serving.handleRequest+0x7b2

 - goroutine 4999 [chan receive]:
    runtime/evictor.(*worker).run+0x1ab
    runtime/evictor.evictLoop+0x5f

(we see a chain where inflight map lock is acquired while evictor is waiting on a different lock - reordering observed in two samples)

End of notes.
